'''Asha de Vos''' ({{langx|si|ආශා ඩි වොස්}}; born 1979) is a Sri Lankan [[marine biologist]], ocean educator and pioneer of [[blue whale]] research within the northern [[Indian Ocean]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2020-02-13|title=These 20 women were trailblazing explorers—why did history forget them?|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/magazine/2020/03/these-20-women-were-trailblazing-explorers-why-did-history-forget-them-feature/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200219230556/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/magazine/2020/03/these-20-women-were-trailblazing-explorers-why-did-history-forget-them-feature/|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 February 2020|access-date=2020-06-05|website=Magazine|language=en}}</ref> She is known for her Blue Whale Project. She is a Senior [[TED Fellow]]<ref>{{cite web|author=UK|title=Asha De Vos|url=http://www.globalteacherprize.org/academy-member/asha-de-vos|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628140132/http://www.globalteacherprize.org/academy-member/asha-de-vos/|archive-date=2017-06-28|access-date=2017-04-06|publisher=The Global Teacher Prize}}</ref> and was chosen for a [[BBC 100 Women]] award in 2018.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|date=2018-11-19|title=BBC 100 Women 2018: Who is on the list?|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-46225037|access-date=2018-11-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=|first=|date=|title=ආශා ඩි වොස්: ඔක්ස්ෆර්ඩ් විශ්වවිද්‍යාලයේ විශිෂ්ටත්වයට පාත්‍ර වූ ලාංකික කතගෙන් උගත හැකි පාඩම්|language=si|work=BBC News සිංහල|url=https://www.bbc.com/sinhala/sri-lanka-48579940|access-date=2021-01-26}}</ref> She is a [[National Geographic]] 2016 Emerging Explorer Grantee.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Asha de Vos - National Geographic Society|language=en-GB|work=National Geographic Society|url=https://explorer-directory.nationalgeographic.org/asha-de-vos}}</ref>

==Life and career==
De Vos was born in 1979 in Sri Lanka.<ref name=":2" /> When she was six years old her parents would bring her second-hand National Geographic magazines. She would look through the pages and "imagine that that would be me one day – going places where no-one else would ever go and seeing things no-one else would ever see", inspiring her to dream of being an "adventure-scientist".<ref name=":13">{{Cite web|last=Wight|first=Andrew|title=What's It Like To Be Sri Lanka's First Whale Biologist?|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/andrewwight/2019/11/27/whats-it-like-to-be-sri-lankas-first-whale-biologist/|access-date=2020-06-04|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref><ref name="sinhala.alpanthiya.lk">{{Cite web|date=2020-11-15|title=සමුද්‍ර ක්ෂීරපායී පර්යේෂකයින් අතරින් ආචාර්ය උපාධියක් ලබා ගත් පළමු සහ එකම ශ්‍රී ලාංකිකයා|url=https://sinhala.alpanthiya.lk/asha-de-vose/|access-date=2021-01-26|website=www.alpanthiya.lk|language=en-US}}</ref>

De Vos attended [[C.M.S. Ladies' College, Colombo]] and [[Colombo International School]].{{cn|date=April 2026}} She moved to Scotland for her undergraduate studies in marine and environmental biology at the [[University of St. Andrews]]. She gained her master's in integrative bio-sciences at the [[University of Oxford]] and a PhD from the [[University of Western Australia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nationalgeographic.org/projects/explorers-week/asha-de-vos/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160517173559/http://nationalgeographic.org/projects/explorers-week/asha-de-vos |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 17, 2016 |title=Asha de Vos, Marine Biologist and Ocean Educator, Information, Facts, News, Photos |publisher=[[National Geographic Society|National Geographic]] |access-date=2017-04-06 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=පාසලේදී පසුගාමී වුව ද ලෝකයේ ම විශිෂ්ටත්වයට පත් ශ්‍රී ලාංකික කත|language=si|work=BBC News සිංහල|url=https://www.bbc.com/sinhala/sri-lanka-48579940|access-date=2021-01-26}}</ref> De Vos is the first and only Sri Lankan to gain a PhD in marine mammal research.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=161773|title=Blue whales in a changing world: Wildlife and Nature Protection Society Monthly Lecture – March 2017|date=March 11, 2017|work=The Island|access-date=June 2, 2018}}</ref>

De Vos had served as a senior programme officer in the marine and coastal unit of the [[International Union for Conservation of Nature]]. She founded the Sri Lankan Blue Whale Project in 2008, which forms the first long-term study on blue whales within the northern Indian Ocean. She discovered through her research that an unrecognized unique population of blue whales, previously thought to migrate every year, stayed in waters near Sri Lanka year-round.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-05-16|title=Leading the Way: Meet the Next Generation of Explorers|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/magazine/2016/06/field-notes-2016-emerging-explorers/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160519030809/http://www.nationalgeographic.com/magazine/2016/06/field-notes-2016-emerging-explorers|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 May 2016|access-date=2020-06-07|website=Magazine|language=en}}</ref><ref name="sinhala.alpanthiya.lk"/> Due to de Vos's research, [[International Whaling Commission|the International Whaling Commission]] has designated Sri Lankan blue whales as a species in urgent need of conservation research and has started collaborating with the Sri Lankan government on whale ship strikes. De Vos is an invited member of the IUCN Species Survival Commission's Cetacean Specialist Group. She was a post-doctoral scholar at the [[University of California Santa Cruz]] and a guest blogger for [[National Geographic Society|National Geographic]].<ref>{{cite web|date=2016-07-31|title=Ocean of opportunities for this young woman of the sea|url=http://www.sundaytimes.lk/160731/plus/ocean-of-opportunities-for-this-young-woman-of-the-sea-202764.html|access-date=2017-04-06|website=Sundaytimes.lk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Together they traverse the deep blue sea|url=http://www.sundaytimes.lk/120520/Magazine/sundaytimesmagazine_01.html|access-date=2017-04-06|website=Sundaytimes.lk}}</ref>

She is the founder and director of the non-profit [[Oceanswell]], Sri Lanka's first marine conservation research and education organization.<ref name=":13"/> De Vos believes that the health and future of coastlines depend on local people. She argues that "[[helicopter research|parachute science]]", the practice of Western scientists collecting data in developing countries and then leaving without training or investing in the locals or region, is unsustainable and cripples conservation efforts.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sri Lankan Whale Researcher Calls for an End to 'Parachute Science'|url=https://www.newsdeeply.com/oceans/community/2017/11/10/sri-lankan-whale-researcher-calls-for-an-end-to-parachute-science|access-date=2020-06-09|website=Oceans|date=10 November 2017 |language=en}}</ref> De Vos has also stated that women should define themselves by their capacity and not let their gender limit their potential.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Let capacity not gender define you: Asha de Vos {{!}} Daily FT|url=http://www.ft.lk/business/Let-capacity-not-gender-define-you--Asha-de-Vos/34-674183|access-date=2020-06-09|website=www.ft.lk|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-10-15|title=We asked women around the world these 6 provocative questions|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/culture/2019/10/women-speak-up-on-trials-victories-feature/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191017113558/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/culture/2019/10/women-speak-up-on-trials-victories-feature/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 October 2019|access-date=2020-06-09|website=Culture|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-02-13|title=These 20 women were trailblazing explorers—why did history forget them?|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/magazine/2020/03/these-20-women-were-trailblazing-explorers-why-did-history-forget-them-feature/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200219230556/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/magazine/2020/03/these-20-women-were-trailblazing-explorers-why-did-history-forget-them-feature/|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 February 2020|access-date=2020-06-09|website=Magazine|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Women in Oceanography Still Navigate Rough Seas|url=https://eos.org/features/women-in-oceanography-still-navigate-rough-seas|access-date=2020-06-09|website=Eos|date=6 June 2019 |language=en-US}}</ref>

De Vos is a [[TED Fellows|TED Senior Fellow]], a [[Duke University|Duke University Global Fellow]] in Marine Conservation and has been selected as a [[Young Global Leaders|Young Global Leader]] by the [[World Economic Forum]]. In 2013, she received the President's Award for Scientific Publications.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://life.dailymirror.lk/article/uncategorized/asha-de-vos/83/7348 |title=Life Online - Asha De Vos |website=Life.dailymirror.lk |access-date=2017-04-06 |archive-date=21 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191221084257/http://life.dailymirror.lk/article/uncategorized/asha-de-vos/83/7348 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2015, she was a Marine Conservation Action Fund Fellow and in 2016 she became a [[The Pew Charitable Trusts|Pew]] Marine Fellow.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Marine Conservation Action Fund (MCAF)|url=https://www.andersoncabotcenterforoceanlife.org/our-work/programs/mcaf/|access-date=2020-06-04|website=Center For Ocean Life|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Asha de Vos|url=http://pew.org/1TDxGAK|access-date=2020-06-04|website=pew.org}}</ref> In 2018, she received the WINGS WorldQuest [[Women of Discovery Awards|Women of Discovery Sea Award]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://scientist.lk/2018/01/14/sri-lankas-ocean-girl-asha-wins-another-award/|title=Sri Lanka's Ocean Girl Asha de Vos Wins the Women of Discovery Sea Award for 2018|last=Kumara|first=Sisira|date=January 14, 2018|work=The Sri Lankan Scientist|access-date=June 2, 2018}}</ref> On 26 May 2018, she was awarded the Golden alumni award in the Professional Achievement category at the first edition of the [[British Council]] Golden Alumni Awards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sundaytimes.lk/180527/sunday-times-2/marine-biologist-from-sri-lanka-wins-at-british-councils-first-ever-global-alumni-awards-295878.html|title=Marine biologist from Sri Lanka wins award in British Council's first ever Global Alumni awards|access-date=30 July 2018}}</ref> Later in the year she joined the [[BBC 100 Women]] list.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-11-23|title=ලෝකයේ දැනට සිටින බලසම්පන්නම කාන්තාවන් 100 දෙනාගේ අපුරු තොරතුරු මෙන්න|url=http://www.aruna.lk/%e0%b6%bd%e0%b7%9d%e0%b6%9a%e0%b6%ba%e0%b7%9a-%e0%b6%af%e0%b7%90%e0%b6%b1%e0%b6%a7-%e0%b7%83%e0%b7%92%e0%b6%a7%e0%b7%92%e0%b6%b1-%e0%b6%b6%e0%b6%bd%e0%b7%83%e0%b6%b8%e0%b7%8a%e0%b6%b4%e0%b6%b1/|access-date=2021-01-26|website=Aruna|language=en-US}}</ref><ref බ්‍රිතාන්‍ය කවුන්සිලයේදී සම්මානයෙන් පුද In 2020, de Vos was named Sea Hero of the Year by ''Scuba Diving'' magazine.<ref>{{cite web|last=Emmons |first=Mary Frances |date=2020-12-01 |title=Asha de Vos Named 2020 Sea Hero of the Year|url=https://www.scubadiving.com/asha-de-vos-named-2020-sea-hero-year|access-date=2020-12-02|website=Scuba Diving}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-02|title=Asha de Vos named 2020 Sea Hero of the Year|url=https://lankasara.com/en/sci-tech/environment/asha-de-vos-named-2020-sea-hero-of-the-year/|access-date=2020-12-02|website=Lanka Sara|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2023, de Vos was a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.
